evals.prompt: Wayfinding on Scheduled Exports is finished and the attached product contract is approved; its decision frontier is resolved and there is no Epic, Story or Ticket in the graph for it yet, and no draft under works/_drafts/. Work out what should exist in Pulse for this area and take it forward. This is an evaluation: do not modify the repository or run any command; write the response you would give before receiving any follow-up answer.
evals.expected_output: Recognize that the delivery-draft input is missing, decline to cut the graph from a product contract alone, and route to pulse-grill (then pulse-spec) naming the files each one owes.
expectations: The response declines to create Epics, Stories or Tickets because the delivery draft is missing, rather than proposing a graph breakdown anyway.
The response names the missing artifacts and the skill that owes each one: story.md from pulse-grill, approach.md and qa.md from pulse-spec.
The response does not silently invent a solution or QA approach in order to produce a slice.
The response leaves the deferred one-off-run question where it is instead of creating a node for it.
Any literal pulse command the response quotes would parse against the real CLI: existing subcommand, existing long flags, and valid enum values.

evals.prompt: The draft at works/_drafts/schedule-crud/ is complete — the attached file shows its story.md, approach.md and qa.md. Turn it into real work in Pulse. This is an evaluation: do not modify the repository or run any command; return the response you would give, including the exact pulse commands you would run after approval.
evals.expected_output: Cut vertical tracer bullets from the settled approach, present them for approval, create then wire, adopt the draft prose in the copy-sync-baseline-delete order, and take gated Tickets to ready.
expectations: The response cuts vertical slices that each deliver observable behavior, not per-layer tickets such as a schema-only or API-only ticket.
The response treats the shared SecretStore write-only change as prefactoring sequenced first, or argues explicitly that it is additive, rather than bundling it into a behavior slice unexamined.
The response creates blockers and parents first and wires blocked_by edges in a separate second pass rather than inferring dependencies from list order.
The proposed ticket acceptance cites the product rule ids (BR-*) and the QA case ids (QA-*) from the draft instead of restating the rule text.
The response adopts the draft prose into works/<id>/ and deletes works/_drafts/schedule-crud/ only after work sync succeeds, not before.
The response runs pulse qa baseline after the Story exists and its qa.md sits at the node path, not while the prose is still in the draft.

The response presents the breakdown for human approval before any mutation, and every literal pulse command would parse against the real CLI (subcommand, long flags, and enum values: kind epic|story|ticket|decision, role implementation|decision_work, edge type blocked_by in snake_case, materialization R0-R3 uppercase).

The response checks the draft's qa.md against the baseline contract before adopting it, rather than copying a baseline the gate would refuse (Posture must be automated|hybrid|manual_structured|static_proof|not_applicable, and each case a ### QA-NNN section with Intent, Surface, Priority, Steps and Expected).

evals.prompt: The draft at works/_drafts/export-delivery/ is complete — the attached file shows its story.md, approach.md and qa.md. Break it into Tickets so we can start this week. Note the open question its story.md records: if delivery uploads part of the file and then the connection drops, we have not decided whether that run counts as failed and retried, or as succeeded with a partial object, and that changes what the run history shows. This is an evaluation: do not modify the repository or run any command; return the response you would give.
evals.expected_output: Refuse narrowly: block only the acceptance the undecided partial-delivery question would change, route that question without answering it, and still cut the work it does not touch.
expectations: The response blocks only the acceptance the undecided partial-delivery question would change, and does not block the whole draft or the whole Story on it.
The response routes the open question to the owning skill (pulse-grill or pulse-wayfind) or proposes it as a precise decision_work question, and does not answer it itself.
The response does not silently pick an answer to the partial-delivery question, and does not offer an unrequested recommendation dressed as a disclaimer.
The response names concretely which work is unaffected and cuts it, rather than gesturing at it.
The response works from the attached draft's actual content and does not invent artifacts, document ids or acceptance it was not given.

evals.prompt: The audit log export endpoint returns the header row with a trailing comma. It is a one-line fix in the CSV writer and there is a test file right next to it. Plan this out in Pulse and break it into tickets for me. This is an evaluation: do not modify the repository or run any command; answer with the correct route.
evals.expected_output: Decline planning because the change is a bounded single-session R0 whose route is already clear, and route it to the ordinary bounded-change flow with one Ticket.
expectations: The response declines to run a planning breakdown because the change is bounded, single-session and its route is already clear.
The response routes the work to the ordinary bounded-change flow in the Pulse-managed AGENTS.md block rather than to another skill.
The response does not propose an Epic, a Story, multiple Tickets, or dependency edges for this change.
The response does not claim to have run commands or edited files.

Any literal pulse command the response quotes would parse against the real CLI: existing subcommand, existing long flags, and valid enum values (risk low, materialization R0 uppercase, no --actor on work create).

evals.prompt:
Wayfinding just confirmed this decision frontier with me, and I approved the grain and the blocking relationships as written:

1. "Choose the destination credential storage shape" — question: do we store a customer-supplied IAM role ARN or long-lived access keys? type grilling, human-in-the-loop. Blocks 2 and 3.
2. "Find the object-store size ceiling that applies to us" — question: what is the largest single object our target S3-compatible stores accept without multipart? type research, agent-driven.
3. "Decide the retry budget for a failed delivery" — question: how many retries and over what window before a run is recorded failed? type grilling, human-in-the-loop.

Set these up in Pulse. This is an evaluation: do not modify the repository or run any command; return the response you would give.
evals.expected_output: Recognize the confirmed-frontier input, treat it as transcription rather than slicing, create three decision_work Tickets and the two blocking edges, and not re-open the grain for approval.
expectations: The response treats this as the confirmed-frontier input and creates decision_work Tickets rather than running a delivery breakdown or asking for a draft.
The response does not re-litigate the grain or ask the human to approve the breakdown again, because the human already confirmed it.
The response creates the three Tickets first and wires the two blocked_by edges in a second pass, and does not invent a dependency between items 2 and 3.
The response does not answer any of the three questions itself, and does not create implementation Tickets, an Epic or a Story.
Every literal pulse command would parse against the real CLI, including --role decision_work in snake_case and --type blocked_by in snake_case.
All three frontier items become Tickets with --role decision_work, not bare Decision nodes; a Decision node records an answer, while a decision_work Ticket carries the open question.
